newsitem.title: UK: UK's Halifax says house prices rose 0.8 pct in Q3.
newsitem.headline: UK's Halifax says house prices rose 0.8 pct in Q3.

text.p: House prices in the UK rose by 0.8 percent in the third quarter from the previous quarter, the Halifax Building Society said on Thursday, compared with the previous quarter's 2.2 percent rise.

The annual rate of house price inflation in the third quarter rose to 5.4 percent from 3.8 percent in the second quarter, reflecting the fact that prices fell between the second and third quarters of 1995.
"Recent months have seen renewed buyer confidence, coupled with a hardening of prices and improved sales," Halifax said.
It said sales in most areas were up around 20 to 30 percent on the same period last year, with price increases propelling many home owners out of negative equity.

The Halifax said last week that seasonally adjusted house prices fell 0.1 percent in September after rising 0.4 percent in August. Annual house price inflation was 5.2 percent in September, down from a previous 5.7 percent.
